sentences.zh: 〖西鄂〗有精山，朱雋破孫夏。山海經曰：「有豐山，神耕父處之，常遊清泠之淵，出入有光，見即其國為敗。有九鍾焉，是知霜鳴。」郭璞曰：「清泠水在西鄂縣山上，神來時水赤光耀，今有屋祠也。霜降則鍾鳴，故言知也。物有自然感應，而不可為也。」南都賦注：「耕父，旱鬼也。」皇覽曰王子朝冢在縣西。

translations.literal: Xi’e: it had Mount Jing, where Zhu Jun defeated Sun Xia. The Classic of Mountains and Seas says, “There was Mount Feng, where the spirit Gengfu dwelt. He often wandered in the depths of Qingling; when he came and went there was light, and if he appeared, that state would be defeated. There were nine bells there, which knew frost and rang.” Guo Pu says, “Qingling Water is on the mountain in Xi’e county. When the spirit comes, the water glows red and bright; today there is a roofed shrine. When frost descends, the bells ring, so it says they know. Things have natural stimulus and response, but it cannot be contrived.” The commentary to the Rhapsody on the Southern Capital says, “Gengfu is a drought ghost.” The Huanglan says Prince Chao’s tomb was west of the county.

translations.literal: Sui: the ancient state of Sui. West of the county was Broken Snake Mound, the snake that held the pearl. Du Yu says it had Lai Pavilion. In Duke Xi 15 of the Zuo Tradition, Qi attacked Li, which was north of the county. The Diwang shiji says, “The Shennong clan arose at Lieshan and was called the Lieshan clan; today this is Li Township in Sui.” The Jingzhou ji says, “On the northern border of the county is Mount Chong, and the mountain has a cave said to be where Shennong was born. There is also a tract measuring one qing and twenty mu around, with two rings of moats outside and nine wells within. Tradition says that after Shennong was born, the nine wells opened by themselves; when one well is drawn from, all the wells move. This place is the shrine of Shennong, and each year sacrifices are regularly offered there.”

translations.literal: Li: a marquisate. The Jingzhou ji says, “Eight li north of the county was Chrysanthemum Water. Beside its source were fragrant chrysanthemums everywhere, and the water was extremely sweet and fragrant. There were also thirty households there; they no longer dug wells but relied on drinking this water. The longest lifespans were 120 or 130 years, middle lifespans more than 100, and those who reached seventy were still considered to have died young. When Wang Chang, Excellency of Works of Han, and Yuan Wei, Grand Tutor, served as magistrates of Nanyang, the county sent more than thirty shi each month, and they used it entirely for drinking, eating, washing, and bathing. The father of Grand Commandant Hu Guang suffered from wind weakness; Nanyang constantly drew this water for him to drink, and the illness was then cured. These chrysanthemum stalks are short and the flowers large; eaten, they are sweet and delicious, different from other chrysanthemums. Guang also collected their seeds and planted them in the capital, and thereafter they were transmitted and planted everywhere.”

translations.literal: Jiangling: the Records of the Historian says that Xiong Qu of Chu established his eldest son Kang as King of Judan; Zhang Ying says this is today’s Jiangling. The Huanglan says, “Sunshu Ao’s tomb was in Baitu Ward inside the city.” It had Jin Township. In Duke Zhuang 19 of the Zuo Tradition, the Viscount of Chu suffered a great defeat at Jin. The Jingzhou ji says, “More than three li east of the county were three lakes. East of the lakes was a watercourse named Chang Valley, and to the northwest was a small city named Yefu. The Zuo Tradition says, ‘The Mo’ao hanged himself in Huang Valley, and the commanders were imprisoned at Yefu.’ More than ten li north of the county was Jinan city, where the kings of Chu made their capital. To the southeast was Ying city, built by Zinang.” In the Records of the Historian, Su Qin persuaded King Wei of Chu, saying, “East of Chu is Xiazhou.” When King Zhuang of Chu attacked Chen, he took one man from a village and returned with him, calling him Xiazhou. Today there is an islet at Xiakou city named Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 〖中卢〗侯国。襄陽耆舊傳曰：「古盧戎也。縣西山中有一道，漢時常有數百匹馬出其中，馬形皆小，似巴、滇馬。三國時陸遜攻襄陽，又值（比）〔此〕穴中有數十匹馬出，遜載還建業。蜀使來，有五部兵家滇池者，識其馬色，云亡父所乘，對之流涕。」荊州記云：「是析縣馬頭山。又縣南十五里有疏水，東流注沔。水中有物如馬，甲如鮮鯉，〔射〕不可入。七八月中好在磧上自曝，膝頭似虎掌爪。小兒不知，欲取弄戲，便殺人。或曰，生得者，摘其鼻，厭可小，小便名為木盧。」

translations.literal: Zhonglu: a marquisate. The Xiangyang qijiu zhuan says, “In antiquity it was the Lu Rong. In the mountains west of the county there was a passage; in Han times several hundred horses often came out from it. The horses were all small in form, like Ba and Dian horses. During the Three Kingdoms, when Lu Xun attacked Xiangyang, several dozen horses also came out from this cave, and Xun carried them back to Jianye. When an envoy from Shu came, there was a man from a five-bu military household at Dianchi who recognized the color of one horse and said it was the one his late father had ridden; facing it, he shed tears.” The Jingzhou ji says, “This was Matou Mountain in Xi county. Also, fifteen li south of the county was the Shu River, which flowed east into the Mian. In the water was a creature like a horse, armored like a fresh carp, which arrows could not penetrate. In the seventh and eighth months it liked to expose itself on the stony flats. Its knees were like a tiger’s paws and claws. Children who did not know and wanted to take it for play would be killed by it. Some say that if one caught it alive, one plucked its nose and it could urinate; the urine was called mulu.”

In the seventh and eighth months it liked to sun itself on the stony flats. Its knees resembled a tiger’s paws and claws. Children who did not know what it was and tried to take it as a plaything would be killed by it. Some say that if one caught it alive and plucked its nose, it could urinate; its urine was called mulu.”

It was attacked and broken by them. In Guangwu’s time it was moved eastward and so was preserved; the name had been changed in anticipation. The Tradition says, “Stopping weapons is wu; a high and level place is ling,” and thus the name was changed.’” Chen Zhao notes: the Former Han was originally named Wuling; it is not known on what basis this response was made. The Jingzhou ji says, “The mulberry tree in the commandery shrine was planted by Guangwu and still exists today.”

translations.literal: Xunyang: it had Zhima Pavilion, where Liu Xun’s officers and troops scattered and settled. To the south was Jiujiang, and eastward it joined to form the Great River. Shi Huiyuan’s abbreviated Lushan ji says, “The mountain is south of Xunyang. To the south it borders Gongting Lake, and to the north it faces the Little River. The mountain is more than thirty li from the Little River. There was a Master Kuangsu, who emerged at the time of Yin and Zhou, withdrew in hiding, and dwelt below it. He received the Way from immortals and shared the ridge with them, so at the time people called the place where he stopped the immortals’ hut and named it from this. The mountain’s great ridges are seven in all, with a rounded base and a circuit approaching five hundred li. Its southern ridge overlooks Gongting Lake, and below it is a spirit temple. The seven ridges join together, and no one has climbed them. To the southeast is Incense Burner Mountain; above it the vapors are thick like incense smoke. In the southwest, before the central Stone Gate, are twin gate towers, with walls standing more than a thousand ren high and waterfalls flowing there. The beauty of its birds, beasts, grasses, and trees and the marvels of its numinous medicines and fragrant woods are famed in their age.” The old records of Yuzhang say, “Kuangsu’s courtesy name was Junping; he was a descendant of Xia Yu.”
translations.idiomatic: Xunyang had Zhima Pavilion, where Liu Xun’s officers and troops dispersed and settled. To the south lay Jiujiang; eastward, it joined into the Great River. Shi Huiyuan’s abbreviated Lushan ji says, “The mountain lies south of Xunyang. On the south it borders Gongting Lake, and on the north it faces the Little River, from which it is more than thirty li away. There was a Master Kuangsu, who appeared between the Yin and Zhou periods, withdrew into hiding below the mountain, and received the Way from immortals, sharing the ridge with them. People of the time therefore called his stopping-place the immortals’ hut, and the mountain was named from it. The great ridges of the mountain are seven in all, with a rounded base and a circuit of nearly five hundred li. Its southern ridge overlooks Gongting Lake, and below it is a spirit temple. The seven ridges converge, and no one has climbed them. To the southeast is Incense Burner Mountain, where vapor hangs like incense smoke. In the southwest, before the central Stone Gate, stand twin gate towers, their cliffs rising more than a thousand ren while waterfalls pour down. The beauty of its birds, beasts, grasses, and trees, and the marvels of its numinous medicines and fragrant woods, are celebrated in the age.” The old records of Yuzhang say, “Kuangsu’s courtesy name was Junping; he was descended from Xia Yu.”

sentences.zh: 〖潜〗左傳曰昭三十一年「吳人侵楚伐夷，侵潛、六，楚沈尹戍帥師救潛」是也。潛有天柱山。

translations.literal: Qian: this is the place in the Zuo Tradition, Duke Zhao 31, where it says, “The men of Wu invaded Chu, attacked Yi, and invaded Qian and Liu; Shen Yin Shu of Chu led an army to rescue Qian.” Qian had Mount Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Qian is the place meant in the Zuo Tradition, Duke Zhao 31: “The men of Wu invaded Chu, attacked Yi, and invaded Qian and Liu; Shen Yin Shu of Chu led an army to rescue Qian.” Qian had Mount Tianzhu.

translations.literal: Linhu: a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Linhu held marquisate rank.

translations.literal: Longshu: a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Longshu was organized as a marquisate.

translations.literal: Xiang’an; Wan: it had iron.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang’an County; Wan was an iron-producing county.

translations.literal: Juchao: a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Juchao was a marquisate.

translations.literal: Lu’an: a kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Lu’an was ranked as a kingdom.

translations.literal: Liao: a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Liao was a marquisate.

translations.literal: Anfeng: it has Mount Dabie.
translations.idiomatic: Anfeng county lay beneath great Mount Dabie.

translations.literal: Yangquan: a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Yangquan was organized as a marquisate.

translations.literal: Anfeng: a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Anfeng marquisate, written with the “wind” graph, appears as a separate fief.

translations.literal: The Kuaiji commandery was established by Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji Commandery dated from the Qin empire.

sentences.zh: 本治吴，立郡吴，乃移山阴。

translations.literal: Originally the seat was at Wu; when the commandery was founded at Wu, it was later moved to Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: The government had first sat at Wu until the commandery was refounded and the capital shifted to Shanyin.

translations.literal: Three thousand eight hundred li east of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: It lay thirty-eight hundred li east of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十四城，户十二万三千九十，口四十八万一千一百九十六。

translations.literal: Fourteen walled places; 123,090 households; 481,196 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen county seats, 123,090 households, and 481,196 people were counted.

sentences.zh: 〖山陰〗越絕曰：「句踐小城山陰是也。稷山者，句踐（濟戎）〔齋戒〕臺。」

translations.literal: Shanyin: The Yuejue says, “Goujian’s small city was Shanyin. Mount Ji was Goujian’s fasting platform.”
translations.idiomatic: Shanyin: The Yuejue says, “Goujian’s small city was Shanyin. Mount Ji was Goujian’s fasting platform.”

sentences.zh: 吳越春秋曰：「句踐築城已成，怪山自至。怪山者，琅耶海中山也。一夕自來，故名怪山。」

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn of Wu and Yue says, “When Goujian had finished building the city, Strange Mountain arrived by itself. Strange Mountain was a mountain in the sea at Langye; it came by itself in a single night, and therefore was named Strange Mountain.”
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn of Wu and Yue says, “When Goujian had finished building the city, Strange Mountain arrived by itself. Strange Mountain was a mountain in the sea at Langye; it came by itself in a single night, and therefore was named Strange Mountain.”

translations.literal: Mount Kuaiji was to the south; on it was Yu’s tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Kuaiji was to the south; on it was Yu’s tomb.

sentences.zh: 山海經曰：「會稽之山四方，上多金玉，下多（瑛）〔玞〕石。」

translations.literal: The Classic of Mountains and Seas says, “Mount Kuaiji is square; above it are many metals and jades, and below it are many fu stones.”
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Mountains and Seas says, “Mount Kuaiji is square; above it are many metals and jades, and below it are many fu stones.”

translations.literal: Guo Pu says there was Yu’s Well.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu says there was Yu’s Well.

sentences.zh: 越絕曰有重山，句踐葬大夫種。

translations.literal: The Yuejue says there was Mount Chong, where Goujian buried the grandee Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuejue says there was Mount Chong, where Goujian buried the grandee Zhong.

sentences.zh: 有浙江。郭璞注山海經曰江出歙縣玉山。

translations.literal: It had the Zhe River. Guo Pu’s annotation to the Classic of Mountains and Seas says the river emerges from Mount Yu in She county.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhe River crossed the county. Guo Pu’s annotation to the Classic of Mountains and Seas says the river rises at Mount Yu in She county.

translations.literal: Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Mao County.

sentences.zh: 〖乌伤〗越絕曰：「有常山，古聖所采藥，高且神。」英雄交爭記曰：「初平三年，分縣南鄉為長山縣。」

translations.literal: Wushang: the Yuejue says, “It had Mount Chang, where the ancient sages gathered medicines; it was lofty and numinous.” The Yingxiong jiaozheng ji says, “In Chuping 3, the southern townships of the county were divided off to make Changshan county.”
translations.idiomatic: Wushang: the Yuejue says, “It had Mount Chang, where ancient sages gathered medicines; it was high and numinous.” The Yingxiong jiaozheng ji says, “In Chuping 3, the county’s southern townships were separated to form Changshan county.”

sentences.zh: 〖诸暨〗越絕曰，興平二年分立吳寧縣。

translations.literal: Zhuji: the Yuejue says that in Xingping 2 Wuning county was divided off and established.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuji: according to the Yuejue, Wuning county was carved out and established in Xingping 2.

sentences.zh: 〖馀暨〗越絕曰西施之所出。謝承書有涉屋山。魏都賦注有蕭山，潘水出焉。

translations.literal: Yuji: the Yuejue says it was where Xishi came from. Xie Cheng’s book has Mount Shewu. The annotation to the Wei Capital Rhapsody has Mount Xiao, from which the Pan River emerges.
translations.idiomatic: Yuji: the Yuejue says Xishi came from here. Xie Cheng’s book mentions Mount Shewu. The annotation to the Wei Capital Rhapsody records Mount Xiao, source of the Pan River.

sentences.zh: 〖太末〗左傳謂姑蔑。初平三年，分立新安縣。建安四年，孫氏分立豐安縣。二十三年，立遂昌縣。東陽記：「縣龍丘山有九石，特秀林表，色丹白，遠望盡如蓮花。龍丘（長）〔萇〕隱居於此，因以為名。其峰際復有巖穴，外如牕牖，中有石林。巖前有一桃樹，其實甚甘，非山中自有，莫知誰植。」

translations.literal: Taimo: in the Zuo Tradition it is called Gumei. In Chuping 3, Xin’an county was divided off and established. In Jian’an 4, the Sun family divided off and established Feng’an county. In year 23, Suichang county was established. The Dongyang ji says, “At Mount Longqiu in the county there were nine rocks, exceptionally rising above the forest canopy. Their color was red and white, and from afar all looked like lotus flowers. Longqiu Chang lived hidden here, and the mountain was therefore named for him. At the edge of the peak there were also rock caves, outside like windows and doors, with a stone forest inside. Before the cliff there was a peach tree whose fruit was very sweet; it was not native to the mountain, and no one knew who had planted it.”
translations.idiomatic: Taimo: the Zuo Tradition calls it Gumei. Xin’an county was separated from it in Chuping 3; Feng’an was separated by the Sun family in Jian’an 4; and Suichang was established in Jian’an 23. The Dongyang ji says, “On Mount Longqiu in the county stood nine rocks, outstanding above the forest canopy. They were red and white, and from a distance all looked like lotus flowers. Longqiu Chang lived here in seclusion, so the mountain was named for him. Near the summit were also rock caves, their exteriors like windows and doorways, with a stone forest inside. In front of the cliff stood a peach tree with very sweet fruit; it was not native to the mountain, and no one knew who had planted it.”

translations.literal: Shangyu: at the end of Han, the southern townships were divided off to establish Shining county.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyu: in the late Han, its southern townships were separated to form Shining county.

translations.literal: Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Shan County.

translations.literal: Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyao County.

sentences.zh: 〖句章〗山海經曰：「餘句之山，無草木，多金玉。」郭璞曰：「山在餘姚南，句章北，故二縣因以為名。」句踐欲遷吳王於甬東，韋昭曰縣東洲。

translations.literal: Gouzhang: the Classic of Mountains and Seas says, “Mount Yuju has no grasses or trees and much gold and jade.” Guo Pu says, “The mountain is south of Yuyao and north of Gouzhang, and therefore the two counties took their names from it.” Goujian wished to move the king of Wu to Yongdong; Wei Zhao says this was an island east of the county.
translations.idiomatic: Gouzhang: the Classic of Mountains and Seas says, “Mount Yuju has no grasses or trees and much gold and jade.” Guo Pu explains, “The mountain lies south of Yuyao and north of Gouzhang, so the two counties were named from it.” Goujian wanted to move the king of Wu to Yongdong; Wei Zhao places this on an island east of the county.

translations.literal: Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yin County.

sentences.zh: 〖章安〗故治，闽越地，光武更名。晉（元）〔太〕康記曰本鄞縣南之迴浦鄉，章帝章和元年立。未詳。

translations.literal: Zhang’an: the old seat, Minyue territory, renamed by Emperor Guangwu. The Jin Taikang ji says it was originally Huipu Township south of Yin county and was established in Zhanghe 1 of Emperor Zhang. This is not fully clear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang’an was the old administrative seat in Minyue territory and was renamed by Emperor Guangwu. The Jin Taikang ji says it was originally Huipu Township south of Yin county and was established in Zhanghe 1 under Emperor Zhang, though the matter is uncertain.

sentences.zh: 〖永宁〗永和三年以章安县东瓯乡为县。

translations.literal: Yongning: in the third year of Yonghe the Eastern Ou township of Zhang’an county was established as a county.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning was created in Yonghe 3 of Emperor Shun from the Eastern Ou township of Zhang’an.

translations.literal: Dongbu: a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Dongbu was organized as a marquisate.

translations.literal: The Wu commandery was split from Kuaiji by Emperor Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun carved the commandery of Wu out of Kuaiji.

translations.literal: Three thousand two hundred li east of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu lay thirty-two hundred li east of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十三城，户十六万四千一百六十四，口七十万七百八十二。

translations.literal: Thirteen walled places; 164,164 households; 700,782 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen county seats, 164,164 households, and 700,782 subjects were registered.

sentences.zh: 〖吴〗本国。越絕曰：「吳大城，闔閭所造，周四十七里二百一十步二尺。又有伍子胥城，居巢城。昌門外闔閭冢虎丘。穹隆，赤松子所取赤石脂也，去縣二十里。有（鹿）〔麋〕湖，欐谿城。又石城，闔閭置美〔人〕山。虞山，巫咸山。」皇覽曰：「縣東門外孫武冢。又要離冢，縣西南。」

translations.literal: Wu: the original state. The Yuejue says, “The great city of Wu was built by Helu. Its circuit was forty-seven li, two hundred ten paces, and two chi. It also had Wu Zixu city and Juchao city. Outside Chang Gate were Helu’s tomb and Tiger Hill. Qionglong was where Chisongzi took red halloysite, twenty li from the county. It had Mi Lake and Lixi city. It also had Stone City and the Beauties’ Mountain established by Helu. There were Mount Yu and Mount Wuxian.” The Huanglan says, “Outside the east gate of the county was Sun Wu’s tomb. There was also Yao Li’s tomb, southwest of the county.”
translations.idiomatic: Wu was the commandery’s old state. The Yuejue says, “The great city of Wu was built by Helu. It measured forty-seven li, two hundred ten paces, and two chi around. It also had Wu Zixu city and Juchao city. Outside Chang Gate were Helu’s tomb and Tiger Hill. Qionglong, twenty li from the county, was where Chisongzi gathered red halloysite. It had Mi Lake and Lixi city. It also had Stone City and the Beauties’ Mountain, which Helu established, as well as Mount Yu and Mount Wuxian.” The Huanglan says, “Outside the county’s east gate was Sun Wu’s tomb. Yao Li’s tomb was also southwest of the county.”

sentences.zh: 震泽在西，后名具区泽。爾雅十藪，吳越之閒有具區，郭璞曰縣南太湖也。中有包山，山下有洞庭，穴道潛行水底，去無所不通，號為地脈。越絕書曰「湖周三萬六千頃」。又有大雷山，小雷山，周處風土記曰舜漁澤之所。臣昭案：此僻在成陽是也。又吳伐越，敗之夫椒，杜預曰太湖中椒山是也。

translations.literal: Lake Zhen was to the west; later it was called Lake Juqu. Among the ten marshes of the Erya, between Wu and Yue there was Juqu; Guo Pu says this was Taihu south of the county. In it was Mount Bao, and below the mountain was Dongting. Cave passages ran hidden under the water and went everywhere, and were called the earth’s veins. The Yuejue shu says, “The lake’s circuit was 36,000 qing.” It also had Great Lei Mountain and Little Lei Mountain. Zhou Chu’s Fengtu ji says it was where Shun fished in the marsh. I, Zhao, note that this is mistakenly placed at Chengyang. Also, when Wu attacked Yue and defeated it at Fujiao, Du Yu says this was Jiao Mountain in Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: Lake Zhen lay to the west, later called Lake Juqu. The Erya lists ten marshes and says Juqu lay between Wu and Yue; Guo Pu identifies it as Taihu south of the county. Within it was Mount Bao, and below the mountain was Dongting. Cave passages ran secretly under the water, leading everywhere, and were called the earth’s veins. The Yuejue shu says, “The lake measured 36,000 qing around.” It also had Great Lei Mountain and Little Lei Mountain. Zhou Chu’s Fengtu ji says this was where Shun fished in the marsh. Liu Zhao notes that this is wrongly located at Chengyang. When Wu attacked Yue and defeated it at Fujiao, Du Yu identifies the place as Jiao Mountain in Taihu.

sentences.zh: 〖海盐〗案今計偕簿，縣之故治，順帝時陷而為湖，今謂為當湖。大旱湖竭，城郭之處可識。

translations.literal: Haiyan: according to the present jixie register, the old seat of the county sank and became a lake in Emperor Shun’s time; today it is called Danghu. In great drought, when the lake dries up, the place of the city walls can be recognized.
translations.idiomatic: Haiyan: the present jixie register says the county’s old seat sank and became a lake under Emperor Shun; it is now called Danghu. In severe drought, when the lake dries up, the outlines of the city walls can still be made out.

sentences.zh: 〖乌程〗左傳襄三年楚伐吳至於衡山，杜預曰在縣南。或云丹陽縣之橫山，去鳩茲不遠，子重所至也。吳興記曰：「縣西北（其）〔卞〕山有項籍祠。興平二年，太守許貢奏分縣為永縣。」

translations.literal: Wucheng: in Duke Xiang 3 of the Zuo Tradition, Chu attacked Wu and reached Hengshan; Du Yu says it was south of the county. Some say it was Hengshan in Danyang county, not far from Jiuci, and was where Zizhong reached. The Wuxing ji says, “On Mount Bian northwest of the county there was a shrine to Xiang Ji. In Xingping 2, the Administrator Xu Gong memorialized to divide the county and make Yong county.”
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng: in Duke Xiang 3 of the Zuo Tradition, Chu attacked Wu and reached Hengshan; Du Yu places it south of this county. Others say it was Hengshan in Danyang county, near Jiuci, the point reached by Zizhong. The Wuxing ji says, “On Mount Bian northwest of the county stood a shrine to Xiang Ji. In Xingping 2, Administrator Xu Gong petitioned to divide the county and establish Yong county.”

sentences.zh: 〖馀杭〗顧夷曰：「秦始皇至會稽經此，立為縣。」史記曰，始皇臨浙江，水波惡，乃西百二十里，從狹中渡。徐廣曰餘杭也。臣昭案：始皇所過乃在錢塘、富春，豈近餘杭之界乎？

translations.literal: Yuhang: Gu Yi says, “When the First Emperor of Qin went to Kuaiji, he passed through here and established it as a county.” The Records of the Historian says that the First Emperor came to the Zhe River, but the waves were bad, so he went 120 li west and crossed at a narrow place. Xu Guang says this was Yuhang. I, Zhao, note that the First Emperor’s route was at Qiantang and Fuchun; how could it have been near the borders of Yuhang?
translations.idiomatic: Yuhang: Gu Yi says, “When the First Emperor of Qin went to Kuaiji, he passed through here and made it a county.” The Records of the Historian says the First Emperor reached the Zhe River, but the waves were dangerous, so he went 120 li west and crossed at a narrow point. Xu Guang identifies this as Yuhang. Liu Zhao notes that the First Emperor’s route was through Qiantang and Fuchun; how could that have been near Yuhang’s borders?

translations.literal: Piling: where Jizha dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: Piling was the home of Prince Jizha of Wu.

sentences.zh: 北江在北。越絕曰：「縣南城，（在荒）〔古淹〕地。上湖中冢者，季子冢也。名延陵墟。」皇覽曰暨陽鄉。

translations.literal: The Northern Jiang was to the north. The Yuejue says, “The city south of the county was the old Yan land. The tomb in Shanghu was the tomb of Jizi. It was named Yanling Ruins.” The Huanglan says this was Jiyang Township.
translations.idiomatic: The northern arm of the Yangtze lay along its northern border. The Yuejue says, “The city south of the county was the old Yan land. The tomb in Shanghu was Jizi’s tomb, called Yanling Ruins.” The Huanglan identifies this with Jiyang Township.

translations.literal: Dantu: in the Spring and Autumn it was called Zhufang.
translations.idiomatic: Dantu was known in the Spring and Autumn period as Zhufang.

translations.literal: Qu’a.
translations.idiomatic: Qu’a County.

sentences.zh: 〖由拳〗左傳曰越敗吳於檇李，杜預曰縣南醉李城也。干寶搜神記曰：「秦始皇東巡，望氣者云『五百年後，江東有天子氣。』始皇至，令囚徒十萬人掘汙其地，表以惡名，故改之曰由拳縣。」

translations.literal: Youquan: the Zuo Tradition says that Yue defeated Wu at Zuili; Du Yu says this was Zuili city south of the county. Gan Bao’s Soushen ji says, “When the First Emperor of Qin made an eastern tour, those who watched the qi said, ‘Five hundred years later, east of the Jiang there will be the qi of a Son of Heaven.’ When the First Emperor arrived, he ordered one hundred thousand convicts to dig up and foul the land and marked it with an evil name; therefore he changed it and called it Youquan county.”
translations.idiomatic: Youquan: the Zuo Tradition says Yue defeated Wu at Zuili; Du Yu identifies this as Zuili city south of the county. Gan Bao’s Soushen ji says, “When the First Emperor of Qin toured east, observers of qi said, ‘Five hundred years from now, east of the Jiang there will be the qi of a Son of Heaven.’ When the First Emperor arrived, he ordered one hundred thousand convicts to dig up and defile the place and branded it with an ill-omened name; for this reason he renamed it Youquan county.”

sentences.zh: 〖安〗越絕曰：「有西岑冢，越王孫開所立，以備春申君，使其子守之，子死遂葬城中。」

translations.literal: An: the Yuejue says, “It had the tomb at West Ceng, which Sun Kai, king of Yue, established to guard against Lord Chunshen. He had his son defend it, and when the son died, he was buried in the city.”
translations.idiomatic: An: the Yuejue says, “It had the West Ceng tomb, established by Sun Kai, king of Yue, as a defense against Lord Chunshen. He ordered his son to guard it, and when the son died, he was buried inside the city.”

translations.literal: Fuchun.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchun County.

sentences.zh: 〖阳羡〗邑。郭璞曰：「縣有張公山，洞密有二堂。」

translations.literal: Yangxian: a town. Guo Pu says, “The county had Mount Zhanggong; its cave was hidden and had two halls.”
translations.idiomatic: Yangxian was organized as a town. Guo Pu says, “The county had Mount Zhanggong, with a hidden cave containing two halls.”

sentences.zh: 〖无锡〗侯国。史記曰：「春申君城故吳墟，以自為都邑。」城在無錫。皇覽曰：「吳王太伯冢在吳縣北梅里聚，去城十里。太伯始所居地名句吳。」臣昭案：無錫縣東皇山有太伯冢，民世修敬焉。去墓十里有舊宅、井猶存。臣昭以為即宅為置廟，不如皇覽所說也。越絕曰：「縣西龍尾陵道，春申君初封吳所造。」臣昭案：今見在，自是山名，非築陵道。

translations.literal: Wuxi: a marquisate. The Records of the Historian says, “Lord Chunshen walled the old ruins of Wu and made them his own capital town.” The city was in Wuxi. The Huanglan says, “The tomb of Taibo, king of Wu, was at Meili Gathering north of Wu county, ten li from the city. The place where Taibo first dwelt was named Gouwu.” I, Zhao, note that east of Wuxi county, at Mount Huang, there is Taibo’s tomb, and the people have honored it for generations. Ten li from the tomb there is an old residence and a well still survives. I, Zhao, think a temple was established at the residence itself, unlike what the Huanglan says. The Yuejue says, “West of the county was the Longwei tomb road, built when Lord Chunshen was first enfeoffed in Wu.” I, Zhao, note that it is now visible and is itself a mountain name, not a constructed tomb road.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxi was a marquisate. The Records of the Historian says, “Lord Chunshen fortified the old ruins of Wu and made them his own capital town.” That city was in Wuxi. The Huanglan says, “The tomb of Taibo, king of Wu, was at Meili Gathering north of Wu county, ten li from the city. The place where Taibo first lived was called Gouwu.” Liu Zhao notes that east of Wuxi county, on Mount Huang, there is a tomb of Taibo, which the people have honored for generations. Ten li from the tomb an old residence and well still survive. Zhao thinks the temple was established at the residence itself, unlike the Huanglan’s account. The Yuejue says, “West of the county was the Longwei tomb road, built when Lord Chunshen was first enfeoffed in Wu.” Zhao notes that what is now visible is simply a mountain name, not a constructed tomb road.

translations.literal: Lou.
translations.idiomatic: Lou County.

translations.literal: The Yuzhang commandery was established by Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhang Commandery was founded under Emperor Gao.

translations.literal: Page 3488, line 10: “Zhang’an, the old zhi/ye; Minyue territory; Guangwu changed its name.” The Palace Edition writes “zhi” as “ye.” Wang Xianqian says that “ye” is correct, and it is now emended accordingly. Now, according to Hu’s annotation to the Comprehensive Mirror, citing Hong’s Lishi, there is omitted text here, and it should read, “Zhang’an was formerly Huipu; Emperor Zhang changed the name. Donghouguan was the old Ye, Minyue territory, and Guangwu changed its name,” which makes the wording complete. The four characters “Dongbu marquisate” at the end of this commandery are instead surplus text. This is explained in detail in the annotation to Jian’an 1 of Emperor Xian of Han in the Comprehensive Mirror. Also, the collected commentary cites Hui Dong as saying that where this has “Minyue territory,” the Treatise on Prefectures and Commanderies in the Song shu has “Minzhong territory.” Also, the collected commentary cites Qian Daxin as saying that according to the biography of Zheng Hong, in the old system the tribute and transport of the seven commanderies of Jiaozhi all went by sea from Dongye. The Dongye mentioned there is Ye county of Kuaiji. Hong became Chamberlain for the National Treasury in Jianchu 8 of Emperor Zhang, and at that time it was still called Dongye, so it clearly was not renamed by Guangwu.

The editors add that Hu’s annotation to the Comprehensive Mirror, citing Hong’s Lishi, says words have dropped out and that the passage should read, “Zhang’an was formerly Huipu; Emperor Zhang changed the name. Donghouguan was the old Ye, Minyue territory, and Guangwu changed its name,” which supplies the missing sense. The four characters “Dongbu marquisate” at the end of this commandery are therefore intrusive text; this is discussed in the Comprehensive Mirror note to Jian’an 1 under Emperor Xian of Han. The collected commentary also cites Hui Dong as saying that where this text reads “Minyue territory,” the Song shu Treatise on Prefectures and Commanderies reads “Minzhong territory.” It further cites Qian Daxin, who notes from the biography of Zheng Hong that the tribute shipments of the old seven Jiaozhi commanderies all crossed the sea from Dongye. That Dongye was Ye county in Kuaiji. Since Zheng Hong became Chamberlain for the National Treasury in Jianchu 8 under Emperor Zhang, when the place was still called Dongye, it plainly cannot have been renamed by Guangwu.
